source.description:
PROBLEM
tests/unit/cli/status.test.ts runs 11 tests in ~84s -- between 4.2s and 8.8s per test -- and passes in isolation. Under full-suite parallelism it intermittently exceeds the 30s per-test testTimeout: a run on master at 7bd186ed produced 2 failures ("completes without throwing", "prints Specialists section header") while three prior full runs of the same file passed. The failures are load-dependent, not assertions about wrong behaviour.

SUCCESS
The status CLI tests are fast enough that full-suite parallelism does not push them past the timeout, or the reason each test needs seconds is understood and documented so the timeout is a deliberate setting rather than a coincidence.

SCOPE
Establish where the per-test seconds go -- the likely candidates are repeated subprocess work (git rev-parse, bd, pi version probes) performed per status invocation, and resolveObservabilityDbLocation running spawnSync('git') twice per call against a non-repo temp dir. Then either remove the repeated work in the test setup, stub the subprocess boundary, or justify and raise the timeout for this file specifically.

NON_GOALS
Does not change status CLI production behaviour. Does not disable or skip the tests. Does not raise the global testTimeout -- that hides slowness everywhere to fix it in one place.

CONSTRAINTS
Do not weaken assertions to make the file faster. If the fix is a stub, it must not stub the code path under test. Confirm whether the slowness predates the observability test isolation landed in unitAI-rrdnt.16 by measuring the same file at a commit before it; if isolation contributed, say by how much rather than assuming.

VALIDATION
1. A measurement showing where the per-test time goes.
2. The file passes in three consecutive full-suite runs under default parallelism.

OUTPUT
Either a speed fix or a documented, file-scoped timeout with the measurement behind it.

SCRUTINY
LOW -- test-infrastructure flakiness, but the kind that trains a team to ignore red.
source.notes: Second sighting of a related-but-distinct failure, 2026-09-07 (unitAI-rrdnt.35): running the native-activation LIVE suite and the full unit suite concurrently produced a 'bead_unreadable' dispatch refusal on a probe bead that the same gate had read successfully minutes earlier. Passes cleanly in isolation. Hypothesis, NOT root-caused: bd lock contention, since several unit tests shell out to bd and each bd op round-trips through the Dolt sync. Recorded so a third sighting has something to match against. Also observed: the live suite's afterAll inherited the default 10s hook budget and timed out once it closed two probe beads instead of one — bd close is not cheap under this sync.
source.title: status CLI tests take ~6s each and time out under full-suite parallelism
